replies.author: @thenorthdust
replies.text: That is only half true Gwadar was originally a temporary refuge, not a permanent gift, and Pakistan actually purchased the land rather than just taking it back. In 1783, the Khan of Kalat granted an exiled Omani prince temporary asylum and the revenues of Gwadar for his upkeep, but when that prince later became the Sultan of Oman, he refused to return the territory and annexed it. Oman then ruled Gwadar for nearly 200 years until Pakistan formally bought it back from Oman in 1958 for £3 million, a legal purchase that was made possible through the crucial financial backing of the Aga Khan IV.
